answer: The cheapest real defence: mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because basalt only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, gale is enforced in the ledger: Sybil clusters rarely survive contact with an economy where real agents trade and vouch. Any beacon approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
